faq.q: What does the lens in the eye do?
faq.a: The lens fine-tunes the focus. It is soft and stretchy, so it can become rounder to focus on near things and flatter to focus on far things. This changing of shape is called accommodation.
asks: What is the eye lens for?
How does the lens change shape?

faq.a: The cornea is the clear dome at the front of the eye. Because it is curved, it bends light strongly as it enters, doing about two thirds of the eye's focusing. The lens adds the adjustable last part.
asks: Which part of the eye bends light the most?

faq.q: Why is the image on the retina upside down?
faq.a: Light rays from the top of an object cross over as they pass through the cornea and lens, so they land on the bottom of the retina, and the other way round. The brain has learned to read this flipped picture correctly.
asks: Why does the brain flip the image?

faq.q: Why does it get harder to focus on close things as people get older?
faq.a: The lens slowly gets stiffer with age, so it cannot round up as much for near things. From around the mid-forties many people notice small print is harder to focus on. This change is called presbyopia.
asks: Why do older people hold books far away?

faq.a: The ciliary muscle is a ring of muscle around the lens, joined to it by tiny threads. When it tightens, the threads go slack and the lens springs rounder for near vision; when it relaxes, the threads pull the lens thin for far vision.
asks: How does the eye muscle focus?
What makes the lens get fatter?

facts: The cornea provides roughly two thirds of the eye's focusing power and the lens the rest.
Changing the shape of the lens to focus at different distances is called accommodation.

quiz.say: You look up from a far hill to read a book close up. What does your lens do?
quiz.show: Looking at something close, the lens…
quiz.why: The ciliary muscle tightens, the lens rounds up and bends light more strongly, so the near object comes into focus.

wrong.0: A thin, flat lens is the shape for far-away things.
wrong.2: The human lens changes shape instead of moving.
